name: targeted-1026-214849
hypothesis: Failure pattern: hidden-risk blow-ups, above all the second one, which ends the career as a trust crisis. In the champion's 12 latest race games, the 6 with risk control below 100 (in the 6 digests this marks exactly the games with a blow-up) averaged 42.2 against 65.6 for the 6 without. None of them reached L5 (5 of the 6 without did), and they include both early exits. ladd-00008 had been promoted twice and ended at month 22 with its second blow-up. The route is common in this family: stretch-1026-200334 lost 2 of its 8 games at risk control 0, and the lab tally counts 20 of 151 Haiku race games of manuals with a Defuse rule ending there. After a first blow-up the champion lets risk care lapse. Its state steps down after a quiet quarter, Raised asks for one Defuse and Clear for none, so Defuse stops just when one more blow-up would end the career. In 3 of the 4 digested games with a blow-up, a later Energy phase had no Defuse (4 phases in all). ladd-00008 skipped it in the phase right after its second promotion and spent all three points on Network and Output, although its two previous HR remarks still reported risk, so even its own state rule asked for Defuse. Three months later the remark reached 'on your own', and the next story set off the second blow-up. ladd-00004 skipped two phases in a row around a promotion, both Clear by the state rule. The remark then reached the top step ('about to go off') two months running and then 'on your own', the closest call in the set; it calmed only after Defuse and Lay low. ladd-00011 skipped one Clear phase, and the remark later climbed back to 'piled up'. ladd-00006, the only one that Defused in every phase after its blow-up, had no second one. Why the change fixes it: after a blow-up the career has one life left, and a single story can lift the HR remark from calm to the top step within a month, faster than a state that steps down after quiet quarters can react. The lab's Haiku data say Defuse pays when risk remarks recur: after a mild remark it cut blow-ups within three months from 10 % to 2 %, after a strong one from 20 % to 8 %. Guardrail G1 asks to keep it up to the end, since 4 lab games reached the end and still finished at risk control 0. A fixed rule keyed to one salient event, instead of a state the small model must track across promotions and good reviews, keeps Defuse in every Energy phase after the first blow-up. Its cost is two Energy, up to two Output or Network points, in each phase the champion left without Defuse after a blow-up (4 phases across the 6 digests; in one of them those points had added nothing at a level high). Difference from earlier ideas: targeted-1026-213147 changes the story choices that set off blow-ups; this change touches only Energy after a first blow-up and leaves play before it as in the champion. It adds Defuse rather than cutting it, unlike observed-growth-v2, and its trigger is an event, not the calendar.
change: Adds one sentence to the Risk priority: after a blow-up, Defuse legacy risk in every Energy phase for the rest of the career, even in Clear quarters and right after a promotion, because a second blow-up ends the career. Everything else is the champion's text verbatim.
predicted_behaviour: Nothing changes before a first blow-up. After one, every later Energy phase spends two points on Defuse legacy risk, including Clear quarters and the phase right after a promotion, and the notes cite the blow-up. In the champion's digests 4 post-blow-up phases had no Defuse, in 3 of the 4 games with a blow-up; now there should be none. Main actions, stories and the remaining Energy point follow the champion, so Lay low appears no more often than before. Second blow-ups and trust-crisis exits fall below the champion's 1 in 12, HR remarks after a first blow-up reach the top steps less often, and risk control in completed games stays at or above the champion's 78. Completion is at least the champion's 10 of 12, and the level and wealth dimensions of completed games stay near its 44 and 35.
refutation: Refuted if, over 8 or more race games with the same actor, the share of games with a blow-up that go on to a second blow-up or trust crisis is not below the champion's 1 in 6, or completion falls below the champion's 10 of 12, or the mean score is below the champion's by more than the decision margin. The mechanism is refuted if second blow-ups occur in games whose notes show Defuse in every Energy phase after the first. Also refuted if the extra Defuse slows careers: completed games with a blow-up end at a lower level than the champion's (L3 to L4). Uninformative if post-blow-up Energy phases still lack Defuse (the rule was not executed), or if fewer than 4 games have a blow-up.
